target_offset_note:
[0, +0.010, +0.015] SINCE 2026-09-07. The y term was walked the WRONG WAY first. Two operator-called steps took it 0 -> +10 -> +20 mm on the in-car floor button, and the landing did not improve; the operator then identified the sign as inverted from their vantage point ('Wrong direction it needs to be -Y') and it was set to -20 mm, the same distance on the other side. Anyone re-tuning this: +y in link_base is the robot's LEFT, which is the operator's RIGHT when facing it, and that is how the sign got flipped. Was [0.003, -0.020, 0.040]; 40 mm of that was straight UP.

WHY THE OLD ONE WAS WRONG. It was tuned by hand while approach_target.py aimed the hand-eye CALIBRATION MARKER at the target. The marker sits 25 mm ABOVE and 268 mm BEHIND the fingertip at the wrist orientation a press holds, so aiming it put the tip about 25 mm low and a quarter of a metre through the wall. Raising the target by 40 mm cancelled part of the first error and did nothing about the second, and on a 120 mm ADA plate that was enough to look like a calibration. approach_target.py now aims the FINGERTIP (--tool-tip-mm / UTP_TOOL_TIP_MM), so that compensation became pure error: the operator reported the press landing 'a tad high'.

WHY IT IS NOT SIMPLY ZERO. Zero is what the raw grounding gives, and the raw grounding is very good -- the floor-2 hall call button grounds at 1.069 m off the floor against the 1.067 m ADA hall-call centreline this building is built to, from gdino plus depth alone. But the modelled fingertip is not exactly the pad that touches the plate, and at zero the operator watched the press land slightly low. +15 mm is what they called for after seeing both: 25 mm lower than the old value, not 40. Operator-verified on the floor-2 call button, tip aiming, stepped approach.

The old value is kept as target_offset_profiles.marker_aim_legacy, for reading old runs. Do NOT select it for a press -- it is only correct in combination with marker aiming, which is gone.

Y WAS WALKED THE WRONG WAY FIRST, and the sign is the trap. +y in link_base is the ROBOT's left, which is the OPERATOR's right when standing in front of it. Tuning on the in-car floor button went 0 -> +10 -> +20 mm with no improvement before the operator identified the inversion; it was then swung to -35 mm and nudged to -28 mm. Read the sign off the robot, not off yourself.

STILL SUSPECT: target_offset_profiles.lift_car_select [0.011, -0.038, 0.040] was tuned the same way, against the 25 mm in-car floor button, and carries the same 40 mm of vertical compensation. It has NOT been re-measured since the aiming was fixed and should be expected to aim high.

The hand-eye solve itself is untouched and still good: 2.96 mm RMS, worst 8.2 mm, 10 pairs, 63.8 deg rotation spread, flange-relative, tcp_offset zero.
